The **2019 ICC Cricket World Cup** was the 12th [Cricket World Cup](Cricket_World_Cup "Cricket World Cup"), a quadrennial [One Day International](One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI) [cricket](Cricket "Cricket") tournament contested by men's national teams and organised by the [International Cricket Council](International_Cricket_Council "International Cricket Council") (ICC). The tournament was hosted between 30 May and 14 July across 10 venues in <England> and a single venue in <Wales>. It was the fifth time that England had hosted the World Cup, while for Wales it was their third.

The tournament was contested by 10 teams, a decrease from 14 teams in the previous edition, with the format of the tournament changing to a single round-robin group with the top four teams qualifying through to the knockout stage. After six weeks of round-robin matches, which saw four games not have a [result](Result_(cricket)#No_result "Result (cricket)"), [India](India_national_cricket_team "India national cricket team"), [Australia](Australia_national_cricket_team "Australia national cricket team"), [England](England_cricket_team "England cricket team") and [New Zealand](New_Zealand_national_cricket_team "New Zealand national cricket team") finished as the top four, with [Pakistan](Pakistan_national_cricket_team "Pakistan national cricket team") missing out on [net run rate](Net_run_rate "Net run rate").

In the knockout stage, England and New Zealand won their respective semi-finals to qualify for the [final](2019_Cricket_World_Cup_Final "2019 Cricket World Cup Final"), which was played at <Lord's> in London. The final ended in a [tie](Result_(cricket)#Tie "Result (cricket)") after the match ended with both teams scoring 241 [runs](Run_(cricket) "Run (cricket)"), followed by the first [Super Over](Super_Over "Super Over") in an ODI; England won the title, their first, on the boundary countback rule after the Super Over also finished level. The total attendance throughout the 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup was 752,000.[[1]](2019_Cricket_World_Cup#cite_note-1) Overall, videos of the group stages amassed over 2.6 billion views from around the world, making it the most-watched cricket competition as of 2019.[[2]](2019_Cricket_World_Cup#cite_note-2)
